match.reason: The closest bank point, mat-bearings-elevation, also covers bearings, so it is broader than this point on elevation and depression alone and its questions may test bearings, which this point does not teach.

draft.title: Elevation and depression
card: Both angles are measured from a horizontal line, the level line through the eye of the person looking.
the angle from the horizontal up to the line of sight, such as looking up at a flagpole top.
the angle from the horizontal down to the line of sight, such as looking down from a balcony to a car.

The two horizontal lines are parallel, so the angle of depression from A to B equals the angle of elevation from B to A. A right triangle drawn from the heights and distances then lets you find the missing length.
draft.remember: Measure from the horizontal: up is elevation, down is depression. The matching pair are equal.

a.q: Priya stands at the bottom of a hill and looks up at a tower on top. The angle between the horizontal and her line of sight is called the:
a.why: Her line of sight goes up from the horizontal, so the angle is one of elevation. Depression is used only when the line of sight goes down from the horizontal.
a.clue: Does her line of sight go up or down from the horizontal?

b.q: From the top of a lighthouse, the angle of depression to a boat is 20°. What is the angle of elevation from the boat to the top of the lighthouse?
b.why: The horizontal lines at the top and at the boat are parallel, so the two angles are equal and the elevation is 20°. 70° is tempting, but that is the angle between the line of sight and the lighthouse, not the horizontal.
b.clue: The two horizontal lines are parallel.
